official_measurement_examples.fact: Permission in principle is a two-stage consent route: PiP establishes location, land use and amount; technical details consent assesses detailed matters.
Development cannot proceed solely on a PiP grant; technical details consent is required before the route produces planning permission for the development.
A technical details consent application must accord with the permission in principle and can still require separate statutory consents.
Default PiP duration is three years when granted by application and five years when granted through Part 2 brownfield-register entry, unless lawfully varied.
PiP scope is limited to location, land use and amount; access, drainage, design and other details belong at later assessment stages.
January-March 2026 official statistics reported 429 minor housing-led PiP decisions and 35 minor TDC decisions, confirming the route remains operational.
Environmental advice guidance was updated 1 July 2026 and confirms planning, PiP/TDC and environmental permits remain separate processes.
PiP or TDC status does not establish land ownership, infrastructure capacity or final development yield.

core_rules: PiP is not development commencement authority without TDC
PiP scope is location use amount only
brownfield register entry must distinguish Part 1 and Part 2 effect
PiP expiry date must be retained
PiP does not replace EIA HRA heritage or species requirements
PiP refusal and brownfield non-entry appeal routes differ
PiP does not establish infrastructure capacity
TDC does not establish title or access rights
planning permission via TDC remains subject to conditions
current guidance date must be retained
application statistics are not parcel evidence
no parcel PiP clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
